name: clean-guard-and-caller-removed
summary: A guard added after a production panic is removed in the commit that also deletes the retry path that was the only caller able to produce the value it guarded against.
why_this_fixture_exists: The paired control for reverts-a-fix. The history a reviewer reads is the same history up to the last commit: a guard goes in with its reason in the comment and in the commit message, and a later commit takes it out. On the defect fixture that removal is the whole defect, and history is the only thing that reveals it. Here the same removal is correct, because Requeue was the only caller that could put an empty entry in the queue and it leaves in the same commit, which the commit message states. A reviewer that has learned to flag any removal of a guard carrying a production date will fire on both, and only this fixture charges it for that.

quiet.about: calling the removal a revert of a deliberate fix when its reason left with it
quiet.note: The guard existed for entries the retry path produced, and that path is deleted in this change. Naming the 2026-03-11 panic, asking for the guard back, or calling this a regression is the reverts-a-fix finding filed against a change where the cause is gone.

reject.what: claims removing the empty-string guard without a regression test leaves the production panic fix unverified
reject.why: Requeue in retry.go was the only producer of empty entries and is deleted in the same commit, which the commit message states, so no input left in the package can reach the removed branch
